prompt: What is the scope of a VPC network in Google Cloud?

choices.text: One region
choices.why: That is a subnet's scope.

choices.text: Global, across every region
choices.why: Right. One network spans every region; its subnets are what is regional.

choices.text: One zone
choices.why: That is a machine's scope.

choices.text: One folder of the organisation
choices.why: A network belongs to a project, and spans regions.

prompt: The planner spreads three machines across zones a, b and c of São Paulo. How many subnets does that take?

choices.text: Three, one per zone
choices.why: Zones never need ranges of their own.

choices.text: Two, for the primary and the secondary range
choices.why: A secondary range lives on the same subnet.

choices.text: None; machines take the network's range
choices.why: A network has no range of its own.

choices.text: One, across the three zones
choices.why: Right. A subnet covers every zone of its region.

prompt: A machine in São Paulo sends to one in Santiago, in the same network. What has to be built between them?

choices.text: Nothing, though the traffic is billed
choices.why: Right. They talk on internal addresses; the crossing is billed at lesson 1's prices.

choices.text: A peering between the two regions
choices.why: Peering joins two networks, not two regions of one.

choices.text: A VPN tunnel
choices.why: A VPN reaches outside the network.

choices.text: A NAT gateway in each region
choices.why: NAT is for reaching the internet, lesson 17.

prompt: What does `gcloud compute networks create planner` make when no subnet mode is given?

choices.text: A custom mode network with no subnets
choices.why: That needs `--subnet-mode=custom`.

choices.text: A legacy network with one range
choices.why: Legacy is deprecated and never the default.

choices.text: An auto mode network
choices.why: Right. `If not specified, defaults to AUTO`, and Terraform's provider assumes the same.

choices.text: Nothing; the mode is required
choices.why: The flag is optional.

prompt: Why was `gcloud compute networks create planner --subnet-mode=custom` refused?

choices.text: The name planner was taken
choices.why: The refusal is about authentication.

choices.text: Custom mode requires a subnet in the same command
choices.why: Subnets are created separately.

choices.text: Compute Engine got no valid credential
choices.why: Right. The lab holds none, so Google refuses before reading the request.

choices.text: The emulator does not support networks
choices.why: The request went to Google, not to the emulator.

prompt: Why can two auto mode networks never be joined by peering or a VPN?
hint: Where do their ranges come from?

choices.text: Every one of them has the same ranges
choices.why: Right. Every auto mode network cuts its subnets from 10.128.0.0/9.

choices.text: Auto mode networks have no routes
choices.why: They have routes like any network.

choices.text: Peering requires global routing
choices.why: Routing mode is not what blocks it.

choices.text: Google forbids it for networks it created
choices.why: The obstacle is arithmetic: the same addresses on both sides.

prompt: What does converting an auto mode network to custom mode fix?

choices.text: Its ranges are renumbered
choices.why: The conversion keeps the ranges.

choices.text: It can then be converted back when needed
choices.why: Custom mode never becomes auto again.

choices.text: It removes the default firewall rules
choices.why: Firewall rules are separate resources.

choices.text: New regions stop getting subnets
choices.why: Right. Unused subnets can then be deleted, but the overlap with other auto networks remains.

prompt: How does the planner make sure its new projects start with no network at all?

choices.text: Deleting `default` after each project is made
choices.why: That works once and depends on somebody remembering.

choices.text: A boolean constraint on the organisation
choices.why: Right. `compute.skipDefaultNetworkCreation` stops the default network being made.

choices.text: A firewall rule denying everything
choices.why: The network would still exist.

choices.text: Creating projects with gcloud instead of the console
choices.why: Both make the default network unless the constraint says otherwise.

prompt: The plan refused `name = "Planner_Santiago"` and `ip_cidr_range = "10.11.0.0/33"`. Who refused them?

choices.text: The provider, on the laptop
choices.why: Right. Both are checked before any request is made.

choices.text: Compute Engine
choices.why: A plan with a placeholder token asks Compute Engine nothing here.

choices.text: The organisation policy
choices.why: No policy was read.

choices.text: The emulator
choices.why: The emulator is Pub/Sub only.

prompt: Every auto mode network takes its subnets from the block 10.128.0.0/___.
How many addresses does a `/24` subnet leave for machines in Google Cloud?
Which change can be made to a subnet's primary range after it exists?

choices.text: Make it smaller
choices.why: A primary range never shrinks.

choices.text: Move it to another block
choices.why: That is a new subnet.

choices.text: Make it larger, into free space beside it
choices.why: Right. The new prefix length must be smaller, and the addresses beside it free.

choices.text: Any of these, while no machine uses it
choices.why: Only expansion exists.

prompt: A staging subnet with `10.10.8.0/21` was added beside São Paulo's `10.10.0.0/20`, and the plan said `4 to add`. What happens on apply?
hint: The provider does not check overlap.

choices.text: All four are created and share the addresses
choices.why: No two subnets of a network may overlap.

choices.text: Google refuses staging, after the rest is made
choices.why: Right. The overlap is checked by Google when the subnet is created.

choices.text: Terraform shrinks the staging range to fit
choices.why: Terraform sends what is written.

choices.text: Nothing is created, since the plan was wrong
choices.why: The plan was valid as far as it could see; the others succeed first.

prompt: Why does `ranges.py` exit 1 when it finds an overlap?

choices.text: Python requires it after printing a warning
choices.why: It is the program's choice.

choices.text: To delete the overlapping subnet
choices.why: It creates and deletes nothing.

choices.text: Because the ranges are invalid CIDR
choices.why: Invalid ranges fail earlier, in ip_network.

choices.text: To stop the apply that follows it
choices.why: Right. A failing exit status stops the next step of a pipeline.

choices.why: That is inside 10.128.0.0/9, where every auto mode network lives.
That is inside the office's range.
10.200 is between 10.128 and 10.255: inside the auto mode block.
Right. It is outside both 192.168.0.0/16 and 10.128.0.0/9.

items: write the subnet in Terraform and plan
trap: Planning before checking is the slip: the plan is clean whatever the ranges, so it proves nothing about overlap.
